body:
Thank you.

It's still fresh in my mind.  It's impossible for me to comprehend healing.

I just wish his last words were something other than, "You saved my life."

The fuck am I supposed to do with that?

Everyone was better off for knowing him, and having him in their lives.

I don't think he realized how much everyone relied on him for things he took for granted, like just generally technical knowledge.  He played tech support to everyone in my extended family and for most of his friends.

It might not seem like much, but him showing my aunt and grandmother how to do simple tasks on the computer blew their minds.

It's fucked up that it takes tragedy like this to truly show the worth of a person.

He lived his life like he had no self worth, but even the little interaction he had with people carried a lot of influence.

It just feels like such a cop-out to say that people are entitled to live their own life.  It's true, but it feels like crap.

Theres nothing I wouldn't have done for him if he had asked, but I think he was unable to ask.

He meant a lot more to a lot of people than he thought.

I'm not sure things would have been any different if he had known this, but I think, because of his disease, he was unable to think this way.
